questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish extensibility from maintainability?
options: Maintainability is about safely changing or fixing existing behavior; extensibility is about adding new capability without rebuilding what already exists -- related but distinct, and a design can be strong on one and weak on the other
They are exactly the same quality attribute
Extensibility only applies to Apex, while maintainability only applies to Flow
Maintainability is a Technical Architect concern, never an Application Architect concern
questions.explain: The lesson gives an explicit example: a design can be easy to safely fix (maintainable) while still requiring a full rebuild to add a new related capability (poorly extensible).

questions.q: What does this lesson say distinguishes a 'plausible near-term change' worth designing for from a purely speculative one?
options: There is no real distinction -- all future possibilities should be treated equally

A plausible near-term change is actually signaled by a stakeholder during requirements analysis, even informally; a purely speculative one has no such signal and is just an imagined scenario nobody indicated
Only changes mentioned in a signed contract count as plausible
Plausible changes are always declarative, speculative changes are always programmatic
questions.explain: The lesson gives the example of a stakeholder mentioning active international-expansion evaluation as a real signal, versus building flexibility for a scenario nobody has actually indicated is coming.

questions.q: Which of these is given as a cheap, deliberate extensibility pattern in this lesson?
options: Hardcoding every possible future value directly into Apex conditional logic
Using a picklist or Custom Metadata Type instead of a hardcoded value when a plausible future value is foreseeable, since it's cheap to extend later
Building a fully generic, configurable framework for every conceivable future requirement before any second use case exists
Avoiding all documentation of design intent to keep the design flexible
questions.explain: The lesson specifically names picklists/Custom Metadata Types, parameterized service methods, lookup relationships, and documented extension points as small, cheap seams -- not large speculative frameworks.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect extensibility to premature abstraction (Lesson 10) and technical debt (Lesson 11)?
options: It argues the three concepts are completely unrelated

It frames all three as faces of the same judgment call about how much today's design should anticipate tomorrow's requirements -- too little anticipation risks expensive rewrites (debt), too much risks unused complexity (premature abstraction)
It argues extensibility always takes priority over avoiding technical debt
It argues premature abstraction and technical debt are the same thing as extensibility
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames extensibility, premature abstraction, and technical debt as the same underlying trade-off viewed from different angles, and calls balancing it the most repeated judgment call an Application Architect makes.

questions.q: What is an 'extension point,' as this lesson describes it?
options: A Salesforce licensing add-on purchased separately
A deliberately designed, documented seam in a solution where a future capability is expected to plug in, costing little to write but saving real time later
A governor limit that applies only to extended data types
A type of Apex trigger exclusive to managed packages
questions.explain: An extension point is a documented seam -- like a comment noting where a second approval path would plug in -- that costs almost nothing to write now and saves real effort for whoever extends the design later.
